## Q9
When you sign up for something like a free e-mail account, you may be presented with a CAPTCHA. CAPTCHA stands for:

## Q9 - Options
(A) Coverage Analysis and Planning Tool for Computers and Humans Apart
(B) Completely Automated Public Turing Test to Tell Computers and Humans Apart
(C) Completely Applied Parallel Technologies for Communication and Hardware Apart
(D) Comparable Additional Protected Turing Test to Tell Computers and Humans Apart

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** ICT (Computers, Internet, Terminology)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q6

CAPTCHA stands for 'Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart'. It is named after the Turing Test, proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, which tests whether a machine can exhibit behaviour indistinguishable from a human. A CAPTCHA reverses this concept — it is a test *designed by a computer* to determine whether the respondent is a human or an automated bot. Common forms include distorted text, image recognition challenges, and checkbox challenges. It is widely used to prevent spam, automated account creation, and brute-force attacks.

## Q12
You and your friends decided to go to Goa after you finish your finals. Your parents set a couple of conditions (see the spreadsheet below).

| Category of condition | Minimum results needed | Actual results | Allowed (Yes/No) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hours spent on homework weekly | 2 | 3 |   |
| Midterm score | 70 | 68 |   |
| Final exam score | 75 | 77 |   |

Imagine your parents care only about the Midterm and Final exam conditions. Which formula can be used to determine whether you are allowed to join your friends?

## Q12 - Options
(A) =IF(C3&gt;=B3,IF(C4&gt;B4,"Yes","No"),"No")
(B) =IF(AND(C3&gt;=B3,C4&gt;=B4),"Yes","No")
(C) =IF(C3:C4&gt;=B3:B4,"Yes","No")
(D) =IF(OR(C3&gt;=B3,C4&gt;=B4),"Yes","No")

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** ICT (Computers, Internet, Terminology)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q27

Since both the Midterm and Final exam conditions must be satisfied simultaneously, a logical AND is required — the student is allowed only if *both* results meet the minimums.

**Option B** — `=IF(AND(C3>=B3,C4>=B4),"Yes","No")` — correctly checks both conditions with `>=` (greater than or equal to) for each.

**Why other options fail:**

- **Option A** uses `C4>B4` (strict greater-than) for the final exam. If the student scores exactly the minimum (e.g., 75 vs 75 needed), Option A would return 'No' even though the condition is met — a subtle but critical bug.
- **Option C** uses an array range (`C3:C4>=B3:B4`) which does not work as a single TRUE/FALSE in a standard IF formula.
- **Option D** uses OR, meaning the student passes if *either* condition is met — but both must be met per the stated rule.

## Q13 - Options

## Q13 - Hint
